VitaNova Pharmaceuticals - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the VitaNova Pharmaceuticals Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during listen-only portions of the call. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss VitaNova Pharmaceuticals' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are David Kim, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Maria Lopez, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Amit Singh, Chief Scientific Officer; Karen Walsh, Head of Commercial; and Greg Foster, Head of Manufacturing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Kim, CEO of VitaNova Pharmaceuticals.

David Kim, CEO:
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. VitaNova delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust revenue growth from our flagship immunology and oncology products, continued pipeline momentum, and effective commercial execution. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives, with a focus on marketing and sales effectiveness where we achieved standout returns, our operating expense discipline amid pipeline investments, R&D priorities fueling late-stage advancements, cash flow strength supporting our balance sheet, geographic revenue diversification with emerging market acceleration, key regulatory approvals and label expansions, and our forward outlook positioning us for sustained growth.

We are particularly excited about our next-generation ADC, NovaTarget, and its potential to capture meaningful share in relapsed/refractory lymphomas and beyond.

Now, I will turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins, CFO:
Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $2.8 billion, an increase of 18% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by strong demand for VitaDerm in immunology and NovaTarget in oncology, alongside contributions from our growing biosimilar portfolio and emerging market launches.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $450 million, or $2.50 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $520 million, or $2.90 per share.

Our operating expenses were $1.45 billion, reflecting continued investment in our pipeline offset by efficiencies in SG&A. Let me provide a detailed walkthrough of this profile, which highlights our disciplined scaling in a high-burn biotech environment. Total operating expenses rose 12% year-over-year and 8% quarter-over-quarter, landing within our guided range of $1.4 to $1.5 billion. This reflects heavy focus on six clinical-stage assets in oncology and rare diseases, balanced by SG&A optimizations through digital tools and outsourcing.

Research and development took 68% at $985 million, up 18% YoY, driven by Phase 3 programs like Nova-301, our HER2 ADC now fully enrolled with data in Q4 2024; Nova-412 bispecific with Regeneron; and Nova-567 gene therapy for Duchenne, ramping CMC for a mid-2025 BLA. External clinical costs hit $420 million, up 25%, from global CRO fees amid supply pressures on vectors—issues peers like CRISPR are facing too. Internal R&D grew 10% to $565 million with discovery headcount up 15% to 450 scientists using AI to shorten timelines by 30%, eyeing two 2025 INDs.

U.S. R&D was 55%, EU 25% with PRIME for Nova-567, Asia 20% leveraging Shanghai but shifting some to India amid NMPA changes. SG&A was 28% or $405 million, up only 4% YoY despite our first CAR-T launch, Nova-289 at $180 million sales. Sales force to 300 reps cost $150 million, payer wins at CVS and Express Scripts $90 million. Outsourcing medical affairs to IQVIA cut headcount 12%, Veeva AI optimizes detailing like at Gilead. G&A up 5% to $165 million on legal for Regeneron amendment. Other OpEx flat at $60 million from a $300 million UK radiopharma acquisition.

OpEx to revenue improved to 220% from 280% YoY on $720 million revenue including milestones. Cash burn down to $1.1 billion annually via CRO deals with WuXi and Lonza, cloud labs cutting reagents 15%, decentralized trials saving 25%. U.S. OpEx 60% amid IRA but biologics exempt; Europe cheaper post-Brexit; China JV caps at 15%. We target non-GAAP profitability by 2027 with $4.2 billion cash to 2028, prioritizing oncology over rare diseases on NPV. Q3 guide $1.4-1.55 billion, FY $5.7-6.0 billion, below industry 20%.

Turning to R&D specifics, expenses hit $452 million, up 15% YoY from $393 million, or 28% of net revenues versus our 25-27% target, with FY guide $1.85-1.95 billion or 22% of $8.5 billion revenues—disciplined versus Regeneron or Gilead. Oncology 42% or $190 million on Nova-ADC-301 Phase 3 at 60% enrolled, Nova-BiTE-045 68% ORR for ESMO. Immunology 25% or $113 million on Nova-TYK2-112 Phase 3 AD complete, data Q2 2025. Gene/cell 18% or $81 million on Nova-GT-DMD-201 RMAT dosing. Emerging 15% or $68 million on AI PROTACs with Insilico, mRNA for NASH. U.S. 55%, Europe 25%, Asia 20% with Hansoh bridging. rNPV guides cuts saving $120 million, in-licenses $250 million, Merck collab $100 million milestones. R&D to 20% by 2026.

Cash position remains strong at $4.8 billion, up 12% from year-end. Balance sheet total assets $18.2 billion up 8% on $1.2 billion SynthoBio acquisition for bispecifics. Net debt $2.1 billion, 1.2x EBITDA versus 2.5x peers, refinanced at 4.2%. Inventory 142 days for label expansions, DSO 52, DPO 78. Equity $12.1 billion up 15%. Operating cash flow $925 million up 28%, non-GAAP $980 million, FCF $685 million up 35% after $240 million CapEx on Suzhou cell therapy. Investing outflows $520 million milestones and deals, financing returned $250 million. U.S. 72% OCF, Europe 18%, Asia 10% up 40%. Enables $1.1 billion R&D, AI trials. FY FCF $2.7-2.9 billion.

Geographically, U.S. 58% or $1.63 billion up 8% on Zynovoq PD-1 and Novalira GLP-1, share 22%. Europe 24% or $672 million up 6% CER on Adalira biosimilar 18% share, CAR-T delays. ROW 18% or $504 million up 28%, emerging 62% thereof. China $178 million up 42% on NRDL Zynovoq, Sinopharm Novalira. Ex-China $162 million up 35% on insulin/trastuzumab. LATAM $92 million up 29% GardivaX, India $48 million up 32% filgrastim, SEA $22 million up 25% RespiShield. $450 million in facilities Suzhou/Hyderabad/São Paulo cut costs 20-30%, 15 filings eight approvals, Access Accelerator RWE, CSPC JV, Biocon co-promo. Emerging 30-35% FY growth to 22% total.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to revenues of $2.55-2.65 billion, adjusted EPS $4.85-5.05, OpEx flat $1.75 billion, 35% margins.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Maria Lopez, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Maria Lopez, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, Nova-ADC-301 advanced in Phase 3, Nova-TYK2-112 enrollment complete, Nova-GT-DMD-201 first doses under RMAT, with upcoming milestones like ESMO data and Q2 2025 toplines. We expect to file multiple BLAs and MAAs in 2025.

Next, Dr. Amit Singh will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Amit Singh, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Dr. Lopez. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research, advancing AI-driven PROTACs, mRNA LNP for NASH, cytokine traps for lupus/IBD, with platforms cutting timelines and partnerships like Insilico yielding new noms.

Now I'll turn the call over to Karen Walsh, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Karen Walsh, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Dr. Singh. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with VitaDerm at $1.2 billion U.S. net, NovaTarget NRx up 35%. Diving into marketing and sales effectiveness, in this competitive landscape like Keytruda or Ozempic battles, our $620 million spend up 12% YoY or 22% revenues matched peers, but ROMI hit 4.2x from 3.8x, above 3.5x IQVIA.

VitaDerm TRx +22% to 1.8 million, NRx +28% to 450k, share 24.5% up 320bps vs Tremfya, persistence 78% via VitaConnect 85% enroll. NovaTarget NRx +35% QoQ to 120k, 15% Hodgkin's share. Reps 2,200 AI-optimized, $1.27 million rev/rep +15%, 28 touches/week 92% complete, P2P 5.2x ROMI 18% conversion on VISTA-2 p<0.001 PASI-90.

Omnichannel 65% digital, portal 1.2 million sessions +42% dwell 4.2 min 16% NRx lift, emails 38% open 12% CTR 22% NRx, DTC 150 million impressions 3.1x ROMI 14% awareness. CAC HCP $1,450 -11%, patient $320 LTV $4,200 ratio 13.1, adherence 72% vs 65%.

U.S. 72% payer 85% lives +7%, +450bps NRx vs TNFs. EU 18% +25% TRx NICE/IQWiG NovaTarget 28% SOV 19% sales. APAC/EM 10% China VitaDerm 40% QoQ 12% share, LATAM $45 million.

PrecisionSales AI $150 million NLP 50 million interactions 30% better actions 62% closes, blockchain samples -22% waste, gen AI emails +15-20% ROMI Q4. Incentives 40% comp to metrics 2.5x productivity. Q4 4.5x ROMI 20% TRx for 20%+ CAGR to 2028 vs UCB.

Finally, Greg Foster will discuss our manufacturing operations.

Greg Foster, Head of Manufacturing:
Thank you, Karen. Our manufacturing operations are running smoothly. Capacity expanded with new Suzhou, North Carolina viral vectors, Hyderabad biosimilars, São Paulo vaccines, efficiencies post-Lonza partnership, supply chain resilient vs COVID issues, focused on CMC scale for Phase 3, blockchain tracking, 15% reagent cuts via cloud informatics.

Now, I'll hand the call back to David Kim.

David Kim, CEO:
Thank you, Greg. Before we open for questions, let me highlight our transformative regulatory wins: FDA sNDA approval for ONC-401 label expansion to frontline NSCLC maintenance on ARCADE Phase 3, 1,248 patients 220 sites, 28% PFS improvement HR 0.72 p<0.0001 to 14.2 months, 4% gr3/4 IRAEs vs 7%, $284 million Q3 sales +42%, $450 million peak add, $75 million milestone, $18 billion market.

EMA MA for GENE-789 SMA Type 2 AAV9 on EMBARK n=156 92% EFS vs 68%, +12.4 HFMSE, RWE 47 patients PRIME, €1.2 billion market €2.1 million dose, U.S. PDUFA Q1 2025 orphan/12yr exclusivity, $320 million peak EU.

PMDA subQ METAB-512 ASCVD expansion CARDIA n=4,512 22% MACE RR HR 0.78 p=0.002 vs semaglutide, +37% adherence, $156 million Japan +31%, ¥450 billion market $200 million peak, NMPA H1 2025.

These via master protocols AI matching adaptive designs, 22% R&D efficiency. De-risk $12 billion pipeline, M&A appeal, four more catalysts.

We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. David, on the regulatory front, how do you see the ONC-401 frontline NSCLC expansion impacting competitive dynamics with pembro chemo, and any color on launch timing?

David Kim, CEO:
Thanks, John. The ARCADE data with 28% PFS lift positions ONC-401 strongly in the $18 billion frontline market. We'll launch immediately with sales force reallocation, targeting 10% share by year-end via KOL P2P on ADCC advantages. Ex-U.S. filings next quarter.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen, JPMorgan:
Great, thanks. Sarah, your OpEx and cash flow look efficient—can you expand on the R&D allocation shifts and FY guide rationale amid oncology focus?

Sarah Jenkins, CFO:
Sure, Emily. Oncology at 42% prioritizes ADCs/BiTEs with >$2 billion peaks, pruning saved $120 million. Cash flow up on Nexara/VitaGLP, FY raised on milestones, runway to 2028 supports 10-15% OpEx growth below peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Piper Sandler. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez, Piper Sandler:
Thanks. Dr. Lopez, thoughts on the gene therapy progress and RMAT implications for DMD?

Dr. Maria Lopez, Chief Medical Officer:
Thanks, Mike. Nova-GT-DMD-201 early durability at 18 months, RMAT accelerates BLA. North Carolina scale mitigates vectors, partnerships de-risk like Zolgensma path.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Park with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Park, Morgan Stanley:
Hi, team. Karen, impressive ROMI—how sustainable is 4.5x Q4 amid FTC DTC rules, and emerging digital role?

Karen Walsh, Head of Commercial:
Lisa, thanks. Gen AI emails, omnichannel 65% sustain it, DTC compliant Clear Skin 3.1x despite FTC. Emerging APAC digital +55% despite forex, PrecisionSales 30% uplift.

Operator:
Our next question from Alex Turner with Jefferies.

Alex Turner, Jefferies:
Sarah, on geographic, what's the emerging market risk from forex/IP, offset plans?

Sarah Jenkins, CFO:
Alex, forex 2-3 points, hedged; IP vigilant post Novartis v Biocon. Local facilities/partners, RWE Access Accelerator drive 30-35% growth.

Operator:
Thank you. One more from Sarah Lee with BofA.

Sarah Lee, BofA:
David, strategic outlook—M&A focus post SynthoBio?

David Kim, CEO:
Sarah, bolt-ons in radiopharma/IO like Harpoon, 4-6x multiples, $2.5 billion chest for synergies, 25-30% CAGR.

David Kim, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Jordan Lee, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the VitaNova Pharmaceuticals Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
